summary: Full backend + frontend testing of Global Early Alert System. 13/13 backend pytest cases passing (REST + WebSocket). Frontend dashboard loads cleanly with map, stats, alerts feed, all filters, sliders, and WebSocket live indicator working. Zero console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: FilterPanel wraps Switch inside <label>: clicking the Switch could fire two onCheckedChange events due to label's implicit click forwarding. Verified data-state toggles correctly via Radix UI primitive.preventDefault, so no functional bug — but consider replacing <label> with <div> to remove the implicit duplicate event risk.

server.py:401 _get_alerts limit hardcoded to 500 in to_list() but /api/alerts query param `limit` allows up to 1000 — limit applied in Python after fetch (items[:limit]); fine for current scale but inconsistent.
Periodic pulse refreshes a random category every 30s (server.py:441) which deletes & re-inserts; under load this can churn DB. Consider TTL/upsert pattern.
WebSocket /api/ws blocks on ws.receive_text() — clients sending nothing keep loop waiting; pulse broadcast still works because it's manager-driven. Fine for current use.
OPENWEATHER_API_KEY absent: app silently uses mock fallback (correct per requirements). No banner shown to user that data is mocked.
test_credentials: N/A — no auth in this app
seed_data_creation: None — backend warms cache on lifespan startup with mock weather/disease/conflict alerts.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend at https://earth-watch-5.preview.emergentagent.com. Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_alerts_api.py -v. Tests cover root, stats, /alerts (combined+filters), per-category endpoints, /predict-risk (anomaly/threshold/empty), /refresh, and WebSocket /api/ws hello. Frontend dashboard verified: stats-header (stat-total/weather/disease/conflict/critical), filter switches (toggle reduces feed; 23→13 when weather disabled), severity-slider (max severity → 5 critical), timeline-slider, refresh-btn, switch-heatmap, alerts-feed cards (clicking opens leaflet popup), and 'Live feed connected' WebSocket indicator. No console errors observed.
